title: Decidability
summary: A decision problem is decidable when one algorithm always halts and returns the correct yes/no answer.

context.note: This node belongs to one explicit foundational presentation; alternate foundations may encode it differently.

assumptions.text: The declared computability theory context is fixed.

content.plain: A decision problem is decidable when one algorithm always halts and returns the correct yes/no answer.
content.exact: A language A⊆Σ* is decidable if there exists a total computable characteristic function χ_A:Σ*→{0,1}.
content.example: Primality testing is decidable even though particular algorithms differ greatly in efficiency.
content.caveat: Decidable does not mean easy; runtime and memory complexity are separate questions.
